title: How to Get the Most Out of the Course
summary: Study-method advice: watch short chunks for understanding, then rebuild the code from memory; take Cornell-style notes; adjust playback speed but don't skip modules; flag hard topics to revisit; and treat getting stuck as normal, solving it with Google and Stack Overflow.

concepts.heading: Key takeaways
points: Lessons are deliberately about 10 minutes each. For longer videos, pause around the 10-minute mark.

Avoid 'code-along' (typing in sync with the video). Watch the chunk focusing on why each line is written, then go to your editor and reproduce it without looking. Recall forces understanding; copying teaches little.
The goal is programming skill, not typing speed. If you want faster typing, practise it separately (keybr.com is suggested).

Cornell notes: one page in four areas: topic at the top, main notes, a side column for keywords/questions/reminders picked out after every few lines, and a summary of the whole lesson in a few bullets at the end. A printable template PDF is in the course resources (also in the reference repo as 01.03 - App Brewery Cornell Notes Template.pdf).
Use playback speed: 2x for material you already know, 0.5x if the pace is too fast or English is not your first language.
Don't skip modules; the curriculum ramps up gradually and gaps make later lessons hard. Videos explicitly marked optional/skippable are the exception.
When a topic is too hard: bookmark it and note the module, retry the watch-then-rebuild method, read around the subject, and come back about a week later. It is usually much easier second time.
Mastery comes from repeated practice, not from watching once.

Getting stuck is normal; working developers spend most of their time debugging. Act like a professional: search Google and Stack Overflow, since someone has almost always hit the same problem. Finding the bug is part of how skills grow.

pitfalls: Typing along with the video at full speed and ending up with working code you can't reproduce.
Skipping modules that look easy, then missing concepts later lessons build on.
Giving up when stuck instead of searching for the error or revisiting the topic later.

playground.coverage: The lesson notes already say to type rather than copy code, to break things on purpose, and to build your own projects.
gaps_and_ideas: Refine the first tip to match the course method: watch about 10 minutes for understanding, then rebuild from memory, instead of only 'type, don't copy'.
Add a 'when you're stuck' line (search the error on Google/Stack Overflow, mark the lesson to revisit in a week) and a printable or on-screen Cornell notes template linked from the lesson.
